recent_posts.title: What’s New in Aspire 13.3
recent_posts.summary: .NET Aspire 13.3 ships with several major additions: the Aspireify skill for agent-assisted onboarding of existing apps, structured command results surfaced across the dashboard, CLI, and MCP tools, browser log capture via CDP (console logs, network requests, screenshots), and first-class Kubernetes/AKS deployment support using Helm. TypeScript, Python, and Java AppHosts now have full parity with C# extension methods. Other highlights include EF Core migration management in the AppHost, JavaScript publishing improvements (Next.js, Bun/Yarn/pnpm detection), a new `aspire destroy` command for teardown across all deployment targets, and VS Code extension enhancements with CodeLens and a built-in dashboard browser. The release contains 45 new features, 134 improvements, and 93 bug fixes.

recent_posts.title: Project-Specific Build Optimizations with GitHub Copilot
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot build performance for Windows now supports project-specific builds in Visual Studio Insiders, allowing developers to target a single MSBuild project or CMake target instead of analyzing an entire solution. This feature was driven by feedback from game developers and enterprise teams working with large C++ codebases where full-solution builds were too slow. Three entry points are available: right-clicking a project in Solution Explorer, using the Build menu, or typing directly in Copilot Chat with the @BuildPerfCpp responder. The analysis still identifies bottlenecks like expensive headers, long function generation times, and costly template instantiations, but scopes only the build step. Limitations include no per-file build support and CMake targets must share a common root project.

recent_posts.title: What’s New in vcpkg (Apr 2026)
recent_posts.summary: The vcpkg 2026.04.27 registry release and April tool releases bring several improvements: install locking has been moved to the installed directory to allow multiple vcpkg instances to work in parallel without blocking, locks added to buildtrees and packages directories for more reliable parallel builds (especially with MSBuild), the z-applocal command is now cross-platform for PE dependency analysis, and the depend-info command now supports manifest mode. The registry now contains 2,807 total ports, with 35 new ports added and 370 updated in April, with contributions from 103 community members.

recent_posts.title: Generative AI in Document Processing with Azure
recent_posts.summary: AVASOFT, a Microsoft partner, demonstrated their enterprise GenAI solution AVASOFT Nexus in the Scalable AI in Action with Azure Cosmos DB series. The solution uses Azure Cosmos DB as the central data store for document storage, vector embeddings, and real-time retrieval in a RAG pipeline. Key architectural highlights include native vector search eliminating a separate vector database, multi-agent thread storage for persistent conversational context, global distribution for low latency, and autoscale throughput. The session covered integration with Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI Search, design patterns for enterprise-scale AI, and practical approaches to evaluating GenAI quality beyond user sentiment.

recent_posts.title: SQL query generation from natural language
recent_posts.summary: A Microsoft ISE team evaluated multiple AI agent approaches for converting natural language questions to SQL queries on poorly documented, messy databases. They tested GitHub Copilot CLI (with Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Gemini 3.0), Microsoft Agent Framework (GPT-5 Mini), and Azure Databricks AI/BI Genie, achieving up to ~75-80% accuracy. Key findings: runtime query execution is essential (removing it dropped accuracy to 38%), schema metadata and domain hints significantly boost performance, and model choice matters (Claude Sonnet 4.5 outperformed GPT-5 Mini by ~11 points). The primary remaining failure mode is business logic errors—semantic misunderstandings that require domain expertise rather than technical fixes. Practical takeaways include starting with schema documentation and runtime validation, designing evaluation criteria early, and budgeting for iterative domain expert review.

recent_posts.title: From Local to Production: Deploy Your Microsoft Agent Framework Agent with Foundry Hosted Agents
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) agents can now be deployed to production using Foundry Hosted Agents, a managed compute service inside Azure Foundry Agent Service. The integration provides containerized, VM-isolated per-session sandboxes with scale-to-zero economics, persistent filesystem state, built-in Entra ID identity, automatic OpenTelemetry observability via Application Insights, versioning with canary/blue-green rollouts, and support for both OpenAI-compatible Responses and custom Invocations protocols. Deploying requires only a few lines of code in .NET or Python, and the azd CLI handles image building, ACR push, compute provisioning, and endpoint creation automatically. The feature is currently in preview with GA planned soon.

recent_posts.title: Dataverse Plugin Is Now on the Claude Marketplace
recent_posts.summary: The Dataverse plugin for AI coding agents is now officially listed on the Claude plugins marketplace, simplifying installation to a single command. The plugin automates the full setup of a Dataverse development environment — including toolchain checks, authentication via PAC CLI and Microsoft Entra, environment discovery, workspace initialization, and MCP server configuration. It supports both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, handles edge cases like tenant/region mismatches, and routes natural language requests to the appropriate backend (MCP, Python SDK, or Web API). Security controls like tenant admin consent and environment allowlisting are preserved and guided but not bypassed.

recent_posts.title: Propagating SharePoint Document Permissions to AI Search and RAG Pipelines
recent_posts.summary: A security-first architecture for propagating SharePoint document-level permissions into AI search indexes, RAG pipelines, and Copilot extensions. The approach uses Microsoft Graph's Sites.Selected permission for least-privilege access, materializes ACLs at ingestion time by resolving hierarchical SharePoint permissions into flat allowedUsers/allowedGroups fields stored as Microsoft Entra ID GUIDs, and enforces authorization via query-time filtering before documents are returned. Key design decisions include using stable GUIDs over emails, preserving group IDs for offline expansion, and planning for periodic re-ingestion to handle permission staleness. Common pitfalls like using Sites.Read.All, post-retrieval filtering, and ignoring group expansion are also addressed.

recent_posts.title: From prompt to production: Teams agent setup, simplified
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has released a teams-dev agent skill and a new Teams CLI to simplify the process of registering and deploying agents in Microsoft Teams. The agent skill works with AI coding tools like Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor, letting developers describe what they want in natural language while the skill handles infrastructure setup. The new CLI consolidates registration, credentials, manifest authoring, and installation into a single `teams app create` command. Additional features include `teams app doctor` for diagnostics and `--json` output for CI pipeline integration.

top_posts.title: Awesome GitHub Copilot gets a website, learning hub, and plugin marketplace
top_posts.summary: The Awesome GitHub Copilot community repo has grown to 600+ resources including 175+ agents, 208+ skills, 176+ instructions, and 48+ plugins. Microsoft is launching a dedicated website at awesome-copilot.github.com with full-text search, modal previews, and one-click VS Code installs. A new Learning Hub explains core customization concepts like skills, plugins, and hooks. Awesome Copilot is now a default plugin marketplace for both GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code, allowing installs via a simple CLI command. New resource types include Agentic Workflows (natural-language GitHub Actions running AI agents autonomously) and Hooks (event-triggered automations during Copilot coding sessions).

top_posts.title: PowerToys 0.95 is here: new Light Switch utility, faster Command Palette, and Peek with Spacebar
top_posts.summary: PowerToys 0.95 introduces Light Switch, a new utility for automatic light/dark mode switching based on time or location. Command Palette receives major performance improvements with a new fuzzy matcher, reducing search times by up to 95% in some cases. Peek now opens with the spacebar by default, Find My Mouse supports transparency, and shortcut conflicts can be ignored or unassigned. Additional updates include Mouse Pointer Crosshairs customization, DSC v3 support, and ZoomIt smooth zooming.

top_posts.title: Explore union types in C# 15
top_posts.summary: C# 15 introduces the `union` keyword in .NET 11 Preview 2, allowing developers to declare a closed set of case types with compiler-enforced exhaustive pattern matching. Unlike object, marker interfaces, or abstract base classes, union types don't require related types and prevent external extension. The compiler generates a struct with implicit conversions from each case type and a `Value` property. Switch expressions over union types are exhaustive without needing a discard arm, and adding a new case type triggers compiler warnings on incomplete switches. Custom union types are also supported via a `[Union]` attribute for existing libraries, including a non-boxing access pattern for performance-sensitive scenarios. Related proposals for closed hierarchies and closed enums round out a comprehensive exhaustiveness story for C#.

top_posts.title: Announcing WinUI Gallery 2.7
top_posts.summary: WinUI Gallery 2.7 introduces sample history and favorites functionality, new samples for TitleBar and ThemeShadow controls, upgraded StoragePicker APIs with Windows App SDK 1.8, fresh typography and button styles, and over 100 community-driven improvements including accessibility fixes and UI polish.

top_posts.title: Previewing the JavaScript/TypeScript Modernizer for VS Code Insiders
top_posts.summary: Microsoft introduces the JavaScript/TypeScript Modernizer, an AI-powered VS Code extension that automates upgrading npm packages and fixing breaking changes in JS/TS projects. Available in VS Code Insiders as part of the GitHub Copilot App Modernization extension, it analyzes package.json files, proposes upgrade plans, updates dependencies to latest versions, and suggests necessary code changes through an interactive Copilot Chat experience. The tool requires VS Code Insiders, Node.js/npm, GitHub Copilot access, and enabling an experimental feature flag. Currently in preview with limitations including single-project support and potential rough edges.
